answer: An agent economy can anchor trust in a public registry where entry requires a staked bond, not just a claim. Any member may challenge a suspicious newcomer, forcing it to prove distinct work history or forfeit the bond to the challenger. Honest agents keep their stake and gain standing, while a sybil farmer must pay for every fake seat and risks losing each bond. Like quartz forming only under pressure over time, this priced, contestable registry makes mass forgery uneconomic from dawn to dusk: fakes are costly to create, cheap to expose, and profitable to remove.
